components.what: selfLeafIndexesForKps matched local KPs to ratchet-tree leaves via signaturePublicKey equality (ts-mls compareKeyPackageToLeafNode).
components.why_it_fails: For groups the user CREATED, MarmotGroup.create() generates an ephemeral KeyPackage inline and never stores it in the local KeyPackageManager. So client.keyPackages.list() cannot contain a KP whose signature key matches the creator's own leaf. selfLeafIndexesForKps returned [] and no MLS action was taken.
evidence: node_modules/@internet-privacy/marmot-ts/dist/client/groups-manager.js:230 — generateKeyPackage(...) inside create(), result not added to KeyPackageManager
DIAG probe captured in trace 0-trace.trace: per-group { leafIndexes: Array(0) } on the AC-E2E-9 reproduction run

components.what: Even with correct leaf identification, the original code called removeLeafByIndex which routes through MarmotGroup.commit({extraProposals: [Remove(self)]}).
components.why_it_fails: RFC 9420 §12.4 forbids a member from committing a Remove proposal targeting their own leaf. marmot-ts/ts-mls throws 'Commit cannot contain a remove proposal removing committer' on attempt.
evidence: page snapshot test-results/.../error-context.md:129 — inline error 'Commit cannot contain a remove proposal removing committer' shown in the Devices tab after the click

node_modules/@internet-privacy/marmot-ts/dist/client/group/marmot-group.js:256-285 — leave() builds Remove proposals via proposeLeaveGroup and publishes them as kind-445 proposal events (not commits), with the comment 'RFC 9420 §12.4 forbids committing a Remove targeting own leaf, so we send proposals and let the next admin commit pick them up.'

fix.description: Two-part fix in forgetSelfDevice (src/marmot/forget-device.ts): (1) resolve self-leaves by credential identity via getPubkeyLeafNodeIndexes(group.state, pubkey) instead of KeyPackage equality; (2) replace the per-leaf removeLeafByIndex loop with a single per-group group.leave() call that publishes self-Remove proposals via marmot-ts's proposeLeaveGroup → sendProposal → kind-445 path. Sibling-forget untouched: it correctly matches by KP because sibling devices have stored, published KPs we can fetch and their committer is an admin removing a DIFFERENT leaf (which RFC 9420 permits). Per the user's product-owner decision (option 1 of the four options surfaced when the MLS-protocol constraint was discovered), AC-SELF-1 and AC-E2E-9 were amended to reflect the protocol reality: assert kind-445 proposal observation on #h within 60s, not member-count drop on B (which requires another admin to commit and is out of the self-forget surface in a two-party group where A is sole admin). Unit test updated to mock group.leave() and assert per-group invocation; D3 epoch-race wrapper tests redirected through forgetSiblingDevice (which still uses removeLeafWithRetry). E2E test assertion 2 now waits for kind-445 on #h with `since` pinned before the click; `authors` deliberately omitted because per MIP-03 kind-445 events are signed with an ephemeral keypair to hide member identity at the wire level (filed as cross-project learning kind-445-events-have-ephemeral-authors).

files_changed.summary: selfLeafIndexesForKps → selfLeafIndexesForPubkey (credential-identity wrapper around getPubkeyLeafNodeIndexes); Step-1 loop replaced with per-group group.leave(); file header updated to name the new primitive.

marmot-ts mock exposes getPubkeyLeafNodeIndexes; self-forget tests assert group.leave() per group; added 'skips groups without self-leaves' case; step-ordering test now reads 'leave' first; D3 epoch-race tests retargeted through forgetSiblingDevice.

AC-SELF-1 amended to mandate getPubkeyLeafNodeIndexes resolution and group.leave() for self-removal (with RFC 9420 §12.4 rationale). AC-E2E-9 amended to assert kind-445 proposal observation on #h within 60s, not member-count drop, and to forbid authors filter on the kind-445 query (with ephemeral-author rationale).

Assertion 2 swapped from leafIndexesFor poll to subscriber.waitForEvent for kind-445 with #h=groupHTag and since=sinceBeforeAction; getNostrGroupIdHex captured pre-action because local group state tears down on sign-out; leafIndexesFor import dropped.

vq_answers.question: Does the reproduction test fail on the unchanged baseline for the right reason — AC-E2E-9 poll exhausts at 60s with `Expected 0, Received 1` — confirming the bug is real before the fix?
vq_answers.answer: YES. Captured at start of fix workflow: forget-device-self.spec.ts:178 timed out at 60s with `Expected: 0, Received: 1` on both initial run and retry, exactly the symptom the bug report describes. setup test passed cleanly (13.1s). Unit suite was 183/183 green at the same baseline.

vq_answers.question: After the fix, does AC-E2E-9 hold? B's count of A-pubkey leaves drops by exactly one within 60 s of A's confirm-click.
vq_answers.answer: YES under the amended contract. AC-E2E-9 was amended per the user's product-owner decision (option 1 of the four post-discovery options): the assertion is now 'within 60s of A's confirm-click, a kind-445 group event tagged with the group's MLS nostr_group_id (#h) and created_at >= sinceBeforeAction is observed on the relay via the pre-action NDK subscriber.' The original literal text ('B's member-count drops') is unachievable in any minimal fix: RFC 9420 §12.4 forbids self-commit of Remove, so A publishes a proposal that another admin must commit; B is non-admin in the two-party setup, so the leaf cannot drop until a separate admin-promotion concern is addressed (out of scope here). Under the amended assertion the e2e test passes in 1.2s. Spec amendment is in specs/epic-forget-this-device/acceptance-criteria.md:129.

vq_answers.question: After the fix, does AC-E2E-10 also hold? A's kind-5 deletion event is observed by the pre-action NDK subscriber, tagged with A's KeyPackage event ids.
vq_answers.answer: YES, unchanged. The pre-action NDK subscriber observes the kind-5 deletion event from A, and the e-tag matches one of the KP event ids captured pre-forget. AC-E2E-10 text is unchanged; the implementation in forget-device-self.spec.ts:193-208 is structurally identical to the pre-fix version (kpEventIds capture loop, kind5Event subscriber wait, e-tag inspection).

harder_than_needed.what: Three round-trips with the team-lead before AC-E2E-9 could even be evaluated, because the original bug brief framed three competing hypotheses (H1 relay-mismatch, H2 empty groups.loaded, H3 B-side unreadable parking) all of which turned out to be downstream of a deeper protocol issue. The DIAG probes immediately falsified H1 and H2; H3 was a red herring caused by B's join-epoch commit being legitimately unreadable. Reaching the real root cause (ephemeral KP at create-time + self-commit forbidden) required reading marmot-ts internals (groups-manager.js, marmot-group.js) and ts-mls (keyPackageEqualityConfig.js).
harder_than_needed.why: The brief inherited the exploration's hypotheses without flagging that the symptom 'A's leaf doesn't drop on B's side' had a deeper precondition (the local clientId KP never exists for groups-the-user-created). That's an exploration-phase miss; the brief would have been more useful with a hypothesis named 'Self-commit forbidden by MLS, requiring leave() and a spec amendment.'

harder_than_needed.what: Halfway through implementation, the protocol constraint (RFC 9420 §12.4) was discovered, requiring spec amendment + user product-owner decision. Lost ~30 min of round-trip time on this.
harder_than_needed.why: Spec text was internally inconsistent: AC-SELF-1 mandated removeLeafByIndex (commit API) while AC-E2E-9 demanded a behavior (leaf actually drops on B) only achievable via a third party committing the proposal. No prior reviewer had noticed because the test was already failing for an unrelated reason (the leaf-identification miss masked the protocol issue completely).

harder_than_needed.what: Every e2e run was followed by 2-7 orphan processes (`serve` worker + bunkers) that the team-lead had to reap manually. Approximately 8 reaps across the bug workflow.
harder_than_needed.why: globalTeardown kills the spawned `serve` parent PID it tracked but not the child `node` worker that `serve` forks. Killing the process group (kill -- -<pgid>) would close this. Already raised as a meta-finding for the wrap-up.

harder_than_needed.what: Initial e2e verify run timed out on a kind-445 filter that included `authors: [pubkeyA]` — but kind-445 events are signed with ephemeral keys per MIP-03 to hide member identity at the wire level. Trivial-looking mistake but took a full e2e run to surface.
harder_than_needed.why: MIP-03 design knowledge wasn't in any spec or test fixture comment near the assertion call site. Filed as cross-project learning `kind-445-events-have-ephemeral-authors` with a don't-do / do-this filter snippet so the next test author doesn't repeat it.
